chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Numan, from Sa'id al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The pilgrim must enter the House before departing; so when you enter it, enter with calmness and dignity, then go to each of its corners.
Then say: 'O Allah, indeed You said, and whoever enters it is secure, so make me secure from Your punishment on the Day of Resurrection.'
And pray between the two pillars that are adjacent to the door, upon the red marble.
If the people are many, face each corner from your standing position where you prayed, and supplicate to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and ask Him.

key_terms.الرُّخَامَة الْحَمْرَاء: The red marble (a specific spot in the Kaaba)
key_terms.الصَّرُورَة: The pilgrim (one who has performed Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended etiquette and supplication for entering the Kaaba according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific Sunnah of entering the Kaaba with tranquility (sakina) and reverence, emphasizing the spiritual significance of the structure as a sanctuary. It prescribes a ritual of visiting each corner (zawa'iy) to offer supplications, linking the physical act to the Quranic promise of security (Aman), while also noting the practical adaptation of facing each corner individually during crowded times to ensure valid prayer and supplication.
